summary.one_liner: A free, in-progress book "Operating Systems: From 0 to 1" and its companion sample x86 OS, teaching bare-metal OS development in C and assembly.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds the source for an book that teaches how to write an operating system from scratch on x86_64 by reading hardware manuals. Parts 1 and 2 cover prerequisites such as x86 assembly, C on bare metal, ELF, linking, loading, and debugging with gdb and QEMU. Part 3 is planned as a set of implementation specifications (chapters 9-13 are marked incomplete) with few code examples. The sample OS in the repository implements protected mode, process creation and management using TSS, interrupts, and the LAPIC, plus a simple keyboard and video driver. Paging and I/O are listed as not yet implemented.
use_cases: learning to write an operating system from scratch
studying x86 assembly and protected mode
debugging bare-metal code with gdb and QEMU
understanding linking and loading without a standard library
following Intel manuals to implement OS components
notable: Teaches by pointing to Intel reference manuals rather than only secondary sources
Part 3 is structured as university-style assignments with implementation specs
Sample OS covers protected mode, TSS process management, interrupts, and LAPIC
No standard library; pure C on bare metal x86_64
caveats: Book is in development; Part 3 chapters are incomplete and future chapters are not yet included
Paging and I/O are not implemented in the sample OS
Prerequisites include C, Linux command line, and basic electronics knowledge
